result.rationale: The diff's poll_feed.rb indeed calls `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`. String#scrub was introduced in Ruby 2.1, and this Dec-2013-era Discourse codebase (unicorn/rails4 lockfile, 1.9-era comments like 'perftools only works on 1.9 atm') plausibly targets 1.9.3/2.0.0 where the method is undefined. If so, every enabled poll run raises NoMethodError, and with `sidekiq_options retry: false` plus TopicRetriever's synchronous `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` path, both feed import and embed retrieval break. The mechanism is verifiable from the diff; the exact Ruby version in CI is not fully verifi

judged_text: `i.content.scrub` calls String#scrub, a method added in Ruby 2.1.0 (released Dec 25, 2013, after this change); on the Ruby versions this repository runs (1.9.3/2.0.0 per its CI matrix and documented requirements) the method does not exist. The first execution with feed_polling_enabled raises NoMethodError (undefined method `scrub' for String), and because the job sets sidekiq_options retry: false the hourly poll fails on every run and no feed item is ever imported; TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve's synchronous `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` path crashes identically, so embed retrieval also breaks whenever feed polling is enabled.

The first execution with feed_polling_enabled raises NoMethodError (undefined method `scrub' for String), and because the job sets sidekiq_options retry: false the hourly poll fails on every run and no feed item is ever imported; TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve's synchronous `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` path crashes identically, so embed retrieval also breaks whenever feed polling is enabled.

adjudication.rationale: In Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed the code does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb). If `i.content` is a String and the runtime Ruby lacks `String#scrub`, this will raise NoMethodError and abort the job; this is amplified by `sidekiq_options retry: false` in the same class, and TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve synchronously calling `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` when feed polling is enabled (lib/topic_retriever.rb), so the failure would repeatedly prevent imports/retrieval. The only non-verifiable part from the diff is the repository’s actual Ruby version support, so impact depends on whether Ruby < 2.1 is used.
